examples.title: Indicator Styles
examples.code:
function IndicatorExample() {
  const [style, setStyle] = useState<'dots' | 'circles' | 'lines' | 'bars'>(
    'dots'
  );
  return (
    <Block>
      <Buttons mb="4">
        <Button
          onClick={() => setStyle('dots')}
          color={style === 'dots' ? 'primary' : undefined}
        >
          Dots
        </Button>
        <Button
          onClick={() => setStyle('circles')}
          color={style === 'circles' ? 'primary' : undefined}
        >
          Circles
        </Button>
        <Button
          onClick={() => setStyle('lines')}
          color={style === 'lines' ? 'primary' : undefined}
        >
          Lines
        </Button>
        <Button
          onClick={() => setStyle('bars')}
          color={style === 'bars' ? 'primary' : undefined}
        >
          Bars
        </Button>
      </Buttons>
      <Carousel indicatorStyle={style}>
        <CarouselItem>
          <Hero color="primary" size="medium">
            <Hero.Body textAlign="centered">
              <Paragraph textColor="white">Slide 1</Paragraph>
            </Hero.Body>
          </Hero>
        </CarouselItem>
        <CarouselItem>
          <Hero color="success" size="medium">
            <Hero.Body textAlign="centered">
              <Paragraph textColor="white">Slide 2</Paragraph>
            </Hero.Body>
          </Hero>
        </CarouselItem>
        <CarouselItem>
          <Hero color="danger" size="medium">
            <Hero.Body textAlign="centered">
              <Paragraph textColor="white">Slide 3</Paragraph>
            </Hero.Body>
          </Hero>
        </CarouselItem>
      </Carousel>
    </Block>
  );
}

examples.title: Controlled Carousel
examples.code:
function ControlledExample() {
  const [currentSlide, setCurrentSlide] = useState(0);
  return (
    <Block>
      <Buttons mb="4">
        <Button
          onClick={() => setCurrentSlide(0)}
          color={currentSlide === 0 ? 'primary' : undefined}
        >
          1
        </Button>
        <Button
          onClick={() => setCurrentSlide(1)}
          color={currentSlide === 1 ? 'primary' : undefined}
        >
          2
        </Button>
        <Button
          onClick={() => setCurrentSlide(2)}
          color={currentSlide === 2 ? 'primary' : undefined}
        >
          3
        </Button>
      </Buttons>
      <Carousel
        value={currentSlide}
        onChange={setCurrentSlide}
        indicator={false}
      >
        <CarouselItem>
          <Hero color="primary" size="medium">
            <Hero.Body textAlign="centered">
              <Paragraph textColor="white">Slide 1</Paragraph>
            </Hero.Body>
          </Hero>
        </CarouselItem>
        <CarouselItem>
          <Hero color="success" size="medium">
            <Hero.Body textAlign="centered">
              <Paragraph textColor="white">Slide 2</Paragraph>
            </Hero.Body>
          </Hero>
        </CarouselItem>
        <CarouselItem>
          <Hero color="danger" size="medium">
            <Hero.Body textAlign="centered">
              <Paragraph textColor="white">Slide 3</Paragraph>
            </Hero.Body>
          </Hero>
        </CarouselItem>
      </Carousel>
      <Paragraph mt="2">Current slide: {currentSlide + 1}</Paragraph>
    </Block>
  );
}

accessibility:
- Uses `role="region"` with `aria-roledescription="carousel"`
- Each item is a `group` with `aria-roledescription="slide"`, named for its place, such as "2 of 6". An item's own `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` takes the place of that name
- Items out of view are `aria-hidden` and `inert`, so screen readers skip them and nothing in them takes focus. With several in view, every item in view is exposed. The copies a loop adds at each end of the track follow the same rule, so where the view runs past the last item, the copies on screen are the ones exposed
- The track is a polite live region, so what comes into view is announced, except while autoplay is moving it (`aria-live="off"`)
- Autoplay waits while the pointer is over the carousel (with `pauseOnHover`) and while focus is inside one of its items, so an item being read or used never moves out of view
- When something else takes the item holding focus out of view (a swipe, a change of width that changes the count, a new controlled `value`, or the item's removal), focus moves to the first item in view rather than dropping to the page
- Navigation arrows have `aria-label` for screen readers
- Indicators use `role="tablist"` and `role="tab"` semantics, one for each position a step can land on
- The Left and Right arrow keys move the carousel while focus is on its arrows or indicators. Inside an item they're left to the item's content, such as a field or a slider
- Previous/Next buttons are properly disabled at boundaries when not repeating
summary: The `Carousel` component provides an image/content slider with navigation arrows and indicators.

parts.summary: The `Carousel` component provides an image/content slider with navigation arrows and indicators.

props.name: value
props.description: Index of the first item in view (controlled); with one item in view, the slide shown. A value between two of the positions a step lands on (see `itemsToScroll`) is shown as given, and the next step goes on from it. With `repeat`, a value past either end wraps around; without it, one that would leave empty space after the last item shows the last full view. Neither correction calls `onChange`. A value that takes the item holding focus out of view moves focus to the first item in view, as a swipe or a change of width does.

props.name: autoplay
props.description: Enable auto-play: one step (`itemsToScroll` items) per `interval`. Without `repeat` it stops at the last position. It waits while the pointer is over the carousel (see `pauseOnHover`) and while focus is inside one of its items, so an item being read or used never moves out of view.

props.name: interval
props.description: Auto-play interval in milliseconds. Default: 5000.

props.name: pauseOnHover
props.description: Pause auto-play on hover. Default: true.

props.name: repeat
props.description: Loop back to the first position after the last. Default: true. With several items in view, the view runs on past the last item into the first ones, so it can show the end and the start side by side. Only loops when some item is out of view.

props.name: hasDrag
props.description: Enable drag/swipe navigation. Default: true. A swipe moves one step, however far it travels.

props.name: itemsToShow
props.description: How many items are in view at once, at every width no `itemsToShow<Viewport>` prop covers. Those props read the way a `Column`'s `size<Viewport>` props do: `itemsToShowMobile` applies below Bulma's tablet breakpoint, each of the others from its own breakpoint up, and where several apply the widest one wins. A whole number, rounded down and at least 1. The widths come from the stylesheet, so they are right on the first paint; the arrows, indicators and steps use the count for the window's width once the page has hydrated, and this one until then. With this many children or fewer, every item keeps its share of the width, nothing moves, and no arrows or indicators render.

props.name: itemsToShowMobile
props.description: Items in view at any width below Bulma's tablet breakpoint (769px), fractional ones included. Falls back to `itemsToShow`.

props.name: itemsToShowTablet
props.description: Items in view from Bulma's tablet breakpoint (769px) up, until a wider viewport's prop takes over. Falls back to `itemsToShow`.

props.name: itemsToShowDesktop
props.description: Items in view from Bulma's desktop breakpoint (1024px) up, until a wider viewport's prop takes over. Falls back to `itemsToShowTablet`, then `itemsToShow`.

props.name: itemsToShowWidescreen
props.description: Items in view from Bulma's widescreen breakpoint (1216px) up, until `itemsToShowFullhd` takes over. Falls back to `itemsToShowDesktop`, and on down to `itemsToShow`.

props.name: itemsToShowFullhd
props.description: Items in view from Bulma's fullhd breakpoint (1408px) up. Falls back to `itemsToShowWidescreen`, and on down to `itemsToShow`.

props.name: itemsToScroll
props.description: How many items one step moves, for an arrow, an arrow key, a swipe or an autoplay tick. A whole number, capped at the count in view so a step never skips an item. Without `repeat`, the last step stops at the last full view, so it can be shorter; with `repeat`, the step after the last position goes on to the first one. The indicators mark these positions, one per step rather than one per item. When the count in view changes with the window's width, the first item in view stays in view.

props.name: arrow
props.description: Show navigation arrows. Default: true. They render `type="button"`, so a carousel inside a form is not submitted by moving between slides.

props.name: arrowHover
props.description: Only show arrows on hover.

props.name: indicator
props.description: Show slide indicators. Default: true. There is one for each position a step can land on (see `itemsToScroll`). They render `type="button"`, so a carousel inside a form is not submitted by picking a slide.

props.name: indicatorInside
props.description: Position indicators inside carousel.

props.name: indicatorPosition
props.description: Indicator position. Default: 'bottom'.

props.name: indicatorStyle
props.description: Indicator style. Default: 'dots'.

props.name: iconPrev
props.description: Icon name for the previous arrow button.

props.name: iconNext
props.description: Icon name for the next arrow button.

props.name: iconLibrary
props.description: Icon library to use.

props.name: iconVariant
props.description: Icon style variant (e.g., 'solid', 'outlined').

props.name: iconSize
props.description: Icon size modifier.

props.name: iconFeatures
props.description: Additional icon modifiers.

props.name: arrowBackground
props.description: Show semi-transparent background on arrow buttons. Set to `false` for icon-only arrows.

props.name: arrowColor
props.description: Color theme for navigation arrows.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.description: Accessible label for the carousel region. Default: 'Image carousel'.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the index of the first item in view when an arrow, an arrow key, an indicator, a swipe or autoplay moves the carousel.

props.name: children
props.description: CarouselItem children.

extraProps.name: ref
extraProps.description: Ref forwarded to the carousel element.

parts.catchAll: All standard <div> attributes and Bulma helper props

props.name: active
props.description: Whether this item is in view. `Carousel` sets it on every item in view, so with several in view several are active.

props.name: children
props.description: The slide's content. An image in it is held to the slide's width at its own height, unless something sizes the image itself: a ratio `Image` fills its frame, and an `Avatar`'s photo its circle, as they do outside a carousel.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes.

props.name: ref
props.description: Forwarded to the underlying element.
